title: नेपालमा बुढ्यौलीको अवस्था {Old Aged Situation in Nepal}
nepali: नेपालको सन्दर्भमा ६० वर्ष र सो भन्दा माथिको जनसङ्ख्यालाई वृद्ध जनसङ्ख्याको रूपमा लिइन्छ । हाल विश्वमा वृद्धहरूको जनसङ्ख्या कुल जनसङ्ख्याको १०% रहेको पाइन्छ भने नेपालको अवस्था ८.१३% देखिन्छ । यस अध्ययनको उदेश्य नेपालमा बुढ्यौलीको जनसाङ्ख्यिक अवस्थाको विश्लेषण गर्नु रहेको छ । प्रस्तुत अध्ययनमा वि.सं. २००९/११ देखि वि.सं. २०६८ सम्मको जनगणनाका तथ्याङ्कलाई स्रोत मानी विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । नेपालमा बि. स. २००९/११ मा कुल जनसङ्ख्या ८२५६६२५ मा वृद्ध जनसङ्ख्या ४०९७६१ (४.९९%) रहेकामा त्यसपछि भएका १०/१० वर्षको जनगणनामा वृद्ध जनसङ्ख्या बढेको देखिन्छ । वि. स. २००९/११ मा जम्मा जनसङ्ख्याको ४.९९% वृद्ध जनसङ्ख्या रहेकोमा वि. स.२०५८ लगभग ४७ वर्षमा सो जनसङ्ख्या १.५१% ले मात्र वृद्धि भई ६.५०% पुगेको पाइन्छ । स्वास्थ्य प्रतिको चेतना, गुणस्तरीय जीवनयापन, पोषणयुक्त खाना, स्वास्थ सेवामा पहुँचका कारण बुढ्यौली वा ज्येष्ठ नागरिकको जनसङ्ख्या र दिनप्रतिदिन बढ्दो क्रममा छ । हाम्रो देशले विकसित देशले जत्तिकै सेवा सुविधा नगरे पनि कल्याणकारी राज्यको अवधारणा अनुरूप वृद्ध भत्ता, सामाजिक सुरक्षा, स्वास्थय उपचार जस्ता कल्याणकारी व्यवस्था गरेको पाइन्छ ।
american_english: In the context of Nepal, the population aged 60 years and above is taken as the elderly population. At present the elderly population in the world is found to be 10% of the total population, while Nepal's situation is seen to be 8.13%. The objective of this study is to analyze the demographic situation of old age in Nepal. In the present study, the census data from B.S. 2009/11 to B.S. 2068 have been taken as the source and analyzed. In Nepal, in B.S. 2009/11, out of a total population of 8256625 the elderly population was 409761 (4.99%), and in the censuses taken every 10 years thereafter the elderly population is seen to have increased. In B.S. 2009/11 the elderly population was 4.99% of the total population, and in B.S. 2058, in about 47 years, that population is found to have increased by only 1.51%, reaching 6.50%. Because of awareness towards health, quality of life, nutritious food and access to health services, the population of the elderly or senior citizens is in an increasing trend day by day. Although our country has not provided services and facilities equal to those of developed countries, welfare arrangements such as old-age allowance, social security and health treatment have been made in accordance with the concept of a welfare state.

australian_english: In Nepal's context, people aged 60 and over are counted as the elderly population. The present study has taken and analysed the census data from B.S. 2009/11 through to B.S. 2068 as its source. In Nepal, in B.S. 2009/11, out of a total population of 8256625 the elderly population was 409761 (4.99%), and in the censuses taken every 10 years after that the elderly population is seen to have grown. In B.S. 2009/11 the elderly population was 4.99% of the total population, and in B.S. 2058, in about 47 years, that population is found to have increased by only 1.51%, reaching 6.50%.
